claim: Inflammasomes are filamentous signaling platforms essential for host defense against intracellular calamities such as pathogen invasion and genotoxic stresses.
source: Inflammasomes are filamentous signaling platforms essential for host defense against various intracellular calamities such as pathogen invasion and genotoxic stresses.
evidence: This is a general statement about inflammasomes supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Dysregulated inflammasomes cause an array of human diseases including autoinflammatory disorders and cancer.
source: However, dysregulated inflammasomes cause an array of human diseases including autoinflammatory disorders and cancer.
evidence: This statement is supported by established scientific knowledge and is consistent with the broader literature on inflammasome-related diseases.

claim: Endogenous pyrin-only-proteins (POPs) regulate inflammasomes by directly inhibiting their filament assembly.
source: It was recently identified that endogenous pyrin-only-proteins (POPs) regulate inflammasomes by directly inhibiting their filament assembly.
evidence: This statement references recent findings in the field and is supported by prior research.

claim: POP1 is ineffective in directly inhibiting the central inflammasome adaptor ASC.
source: We find here that POP1 is ineffective in directly inhibiting the central inflammasome adaptor ASC.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from cellular imaging and FRET assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: POP1 acts as a decoy and targets the assembly of upstream receptor pyrin-domain (PYD) filaments such as those of AIM2, IFI16, NLRP3, and NLRP6.
source: Instead, POP1 acts as a decoy and targets the assembly of upstream receptor pyrin-domain (PYD) filaments such as those of AIM2, IFI16, NLRP3, and NLRP6.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from cellular imaging, FRET assays, and nsEM presented in the manuscript.

claim: POP2 directly suppresses the nucleation of ASC.
source: Moreover, not only does POP2 directly suppress the nucleation of ASC, but it can also inhibit the elongation of receptor filaments.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from FRET assays showing prolonged lag phases in ASC polymerization.

claim: POP2 can inhibit the elongation of receptor filaments.
source: Moreover, not only does POP2 directly suppress the nucleation of ASC, but it can also inhibit the elongation of receptor filaments.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from FRET assays and nsEM showing effects on filament elongation.

claim: POP3 inhibits the elongation of AIM2 and NLRP6 filaments.
source: In addition to inhibiting the elongation of AIM2 and NLRP6 filaments, POP3 potently suppresses the nucleation of ASC.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from FRET assays and nsEM showing effects on filament elongation.

claim: POP3 potently suppresses the nucleation of ASC.
source: In addition to inhibiting the elongation of AIM2 and NLRP6 filaments, POP3 potently suppresses the nucleation of ASC.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from FRET assays showing prolonged lag phases in ASC polymerization.

claim: A combination of favorable and unfavorable interactions between POPs and PYDs is necessary for effective recognition and inhibition.
source: Our Rosetta analyses and biochemical experiments consistently suggest that a combination of favorable and unfavorable interactions between POPs and PYDs is necessary for effective recognition and inhibition.
evidence: This claim is supported by Rosetta computational analyses and biochemical experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: Inflammasomes transduce signals by sequentially assembling filamentous oligomers, with multiple initial pathways progressively converging at downstream assemblies.
source: Inflammasomes transduce signals by sequentially assembling filamentous oligomers, with multiple initial pathways progressively converging at downstream assemblies (Broz and Dixit, 2016; Kagan et al., 2014; Lu and Wu, 2015; Zheng et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Molecular signatures arising from various pathogenic conditions induce the oligomerization of inflammasome receptors, resulting in filament assembly by their pyrin-domains (PYDs).
source: For instance, an array of molecular signatures arising from various pathogenic conditions induces the oligomerization of inflammasome receptors, resulting in filament assembly by their pyrin-domains (PYDs; e.g. viral nucleic acids, reactive oxygen species, specific lipids from damaged mitochondria, and disruption of the trans-Golgi network) (Andreeva et al., 2021; Fernandes-Alnemri et al., 2009; Hornung et al., 2009; Iyer et al., 2013; Roberts et al., 2009; Zhong et al., 2013)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: PYDs are ~100 amino acid (a.a.) 6-helix bundle proteins that belong to the death-domain (DD) family often found in apoptotic and inflammatory signaling pathways.
source: PYDs are ~100 amino acid (a.a.) 6-helix bundle proteins that belong to the death-domain (DD) family often found in apoptotic and inflammatory signaling pathways (Park et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Upstream PYD oligomers induce the filament assembly by the PYD of the central adaptor ASC (ASCPYD), resulting in oligomerization/filamentation of its CARD.
source: The upstream PYD oligomers then induce the filament assembly by the PYD of the central adaptor ASC (ASCPYD), resulting in oligomerization/filamentation of its CARD (ASC: apoptosis-associated speck-forming protein-containing caspase-recruiting domain [CARD]) (Broz and Dixit, 2016; Kagan et al., 2014; Lu et al., 2014; Lu and Wu, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: ASCCARD oligomers recruit pro-caspase-1 and induce its filament assembly, activating the enzyme by proximity-induced auto-proteolysis.
source: Finally, ASCCARD oligomers recruit pro-caspase-1 and induce its filament assembly, activating the enzyme by proximity-induced auto-proteolysis (Broz and Dixit, 2016; Kagan et al., 2014; Lu et al., 2014; Lu and Wu, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Caspase-1 executes two key innate immune responses: the cleavage/maturation of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin-1β (IL-1β) and IL-18, and the initiation of pyroptosis.
source: Caspase-1 executes two key innate immune responses, namely the cleavage/maturation of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin-1β (IL-1β) and IL-18, and the initiation of pyroptosis (Broz and Dixit, 2016; Kagan et al., 2014; Lu et al., 2014; Lu and Wu, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: A hallmark of inflammasome assembly is its binary (on-or-off) nature.
source: A hallmark of inflammasome assembly is its binary (on-or-off) nature (Cai et al., 2014; Franklin et al., 2014; Matyszewski et al., 2018; Shen et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Once assembled, inflammasomes do not dissociate.
source: That is, once assembled, inflammasomes do not dissociate (Franklin et al., 2014; Matyszewski et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Multiple positive feedback loops between upstream receptors and ASC bolster the assembly and result in prion-like self-perpetuation.
source: Moreover, multiple positive feedback loops between upstream receptors and ASC not only bolster the assembly, but also result in prion-like self-perpetuation (Cai et al., 2014; Matyszewski et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The inherently irreversible assembly mechanism of inflammasomes necessitates extrinsic factors to prevent persistent activities.
source: Such an inherently irreversible assembly mechanism in turn would necessitate extrinsic factors to prevent persistent activities.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the irreversible nature of inflammasome assembly.

claim: Mammalian pyrin-only-proteins (POPs) have emerged as major inhibitors of inflammasomes.
source: Indeed, mammalian pyrin-only-proteins (POPs) have emerged as major inhibitors of inflammasomes (de Almeida et al., 2015; Khare et al., 2014; Periasamy et al., 2017; Ratsimandresy et al., 2017)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: POPs function analogously to CARD-only proteins (COPs) that interfere with the oligomerization/activation of pro-caspases.
source: Indeed, mammalian pyrin-only-proteins (POPs) have emerged as major inhibitors of inflammasomes (de Almeida et al., 2015; Khare et al., 2014; Periasamy et al., 2017; Ratsimandresy et al., 2017), functioning analogous to CARD-only proteins (COPs) that interfere with the oligomerization/activation of pro-caspases (Devi et al., 2020; Indramohan et al., 2018; Lu et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The target specificities of POPs are proposed to be dictated by their a.a. sequence homologies to inflammasome PYDs.
source: It has been proposed that the target specificities of POPs are dictated by their a.a. sequence homologies to inflammasome PYDs (Devi et al., 2020; Indramohan et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: POP1 is most homologous to ASCPYD (65% sequence identity).
source: For example, POP1 is most homologous to ASCPYD (65% sequence identity; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This statement is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: POP1 is thought to directly inhibit the nucleation of the ASCPYD filament.
source: For example, POP1 is most homologous to ASCPYD (65% sequence identity; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) and thought to directly inhibit the nucleation of the ASCPYD filament (de Almeida et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: POP2 shares 68% sequence identity to the PYD of Nod-like receptor containing a PYD-2 (NLRP2PYD).
source: POP2 shares 68% sequence identity to the PYD of Nod-like receptor containing a PYD-2 (NLRP2PYD; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This statement is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The primary target of POP2 is thought to be ASC, but it is also implicated in inhibiting the absent-in-melanoma-2 (AIM2) receptor.
source: the primary target of POP2 is thought to be ASC, but it is also implicated in inhibiting the absent-in-melanoma-2 (AIM2) receptor (Periasamy et al., 2017; Ratsimandresy et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: POP3 is most similar to AIM2PYD (67% sequence identity).
source: Finally, POP3 is most similar to AIM2PYD (67% sequence identity, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This statement is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: POP3 targets AIM2-like receptors (ALRs, e.g. AIM2 and interferon inducible protein 16 [IFI16]).
source: Finally, POP3 is most similar to AIM2PYD (67% sequence identity, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C) and targets AIM2-like receptors (ALRs, e.g. AIM2 and interferon inducible protein 16 [IFI16]) (Khare et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Inflammasome filaments entail at least two distinct steps for assembly: rate-limiting nucleation followed by elongation.
source: Inflammasome filaments are highly ordered supra-structures that entail at least two distinct steps for assembly: rate-limiting nucleation followed by elongation (Kagan et al., 2014; Lu et al., 2014; Lu and Wu, 2015; Matyszewski et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The PYDs of upstream receptors do not display significant a.a. sequence homologies.
source: Moreover, although the PYDs of upstream receptors do not display significant a.a. sequence homologies (Kagan et al., 2014; Lu et al., 2014; Lu and Wu, 2015)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: All upstream receptor PYDs assemble into structurally congruent helical filaments and signal through the common ASC adaptor.
source: Moreover, although the PYDs of upstream receptors do not display significant a.a. sequence homologies (Kagan et al., 2014; Lu et al., 2014; Lu and Wu, 2015), they all assemble into structurally congruent helical filaments and signal through the common ASC adaptor, suggesting a degenerate-code-like recognition mechanism (Hochheiser et al., 2022a; Kagan et al., 2014; Lu et al., 2014; Lu and Wu, 2015; Matyszewski et al., 2021; Shen et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The structural similarity of upstream receptor PYDs suggests a degenerate-code-like recognition mechanism.
source: Moreover, although the PYDs of upstream receptors do not display significant a.a. sequence homologies (Kagan et al., 2014; Lu et al., 2014; Lu and Wu, 2015), they all assemble into structurally congruent helical filaments and signal through the common ASC adaptor, suggesting a degenerate-code-like recognition mechanism (Hochheiser et al., 2022a; Kagan et al., 2014; Lu et al., 2014; Lu and Wu, 2015; Matyszewski et al., 2021; Shen et al., 2019).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural data cited from prior research.

claim: PYDs assemble into helical filaments in which each protomer provides six unique protein-protein interaction surfaces.
source: Briefly, PYDs assemble into helical filaments in which each protomer provides six unique protein-protein interaction surfaces (e.g. Figure 1A, 'Type' 1a/b, 2a/b, and 3a/b) (Lu et al., 2014; Lu and Wu, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Individual AIM2PYD and ASCPYD filaments assemble bidirectionally (i.e. extending from both top and bottom surfaces).
source: We found previously that individual AIM2PYD and ASCPYD filaments assemble bidirectionally (i.e. extending from both top and bottom surfaces), with each pair of filament interface types contributing symmetric ∆Gs (e.g. both Type 1a and Type 1b surface show ∆G=–22.1 for ASCPYD•ASCPYD in Figure 1B; Matyszewski et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Each pair of filament interface types contributes symmetric ∆Gs in AIM2PYD and ASCPYD filaments.
source: We found previously that individual AIM2PYD and ASCPYD filaments assemble bidirectionally (i.e. extending from both top and bottom surfaces), with each pair of filament interface types contributing symmetric ∆Gs (e.g. both Type 1a and Type 1b surface show ∆G=–22.1 for ASCPYD•ASCPYD in Figure 1B; Matyszewski et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Bidirectional assembly is universal to all PYD filaments.
source: The interface analysis results from other inflammasome PYDs also showed similar symmetric energy landscapes (Figure 1B–F, left), suggesting that bidirectional assembly is universal to all PYD filaments.
evidence: This is an inference based on Rosetta interface analysis data shown in Figure 1B–F.

claim: The overall ∆Gs for individual PYD filaments are more favorable than those from any putative POP•PYD interactions.
source: We next noted that the overall ∆Gs for individual PYD filaments were more favorable than those from any putative POP•PYD interactions, which in turn suggested that excess POPs might be necessary to inhibit the assembly of inflammasome PYDs (e.g. the sum of ASCPYD•ASCPYD interactions on the top half yields ∆G=–35.9, while that of POP1•ASCPYD is –24.7; Figure 1B–F).
evidence: This statement is based on Rosetta interface analysis data shown in Figure 1B–F.

claim: Excess POPs might be necessary to inhibit the assembly of inflammasome PYDs.
source: We next noted that the overall ∆Gs for individual PYD filaments were more favorable than those from any putative POP•PYD interactions, which in turn suggested that excess POPs might be necessary to inhibit the assembly of inflammasome PYDs (e.g. the sum of ASCPYD•ASCPYD interactions on the top half yields ∆G=–35.9, while that of POP1•ASCPYD is –24.7; Figure 1B–F).
evidence: This is an inference based on Rosetta interface analysis data shown in Figure 1B–F.

claim: POP1 showed more favorable overall ∆Gs for ASCPYD compared to POP2 or POP3.
source: POP1 showed more favorable overall ∆Gs for ASCPYD compared to POP2 or POP3 (Figure 1B)
evidence: This statement is based on Rosetta interface analysis data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: POP2 can inhibit ASCPYD more potently than POP1 in vivo.
source: However, although it was reported that POP2 can inhibit ASCPYD more potently than POP1 in vivo (Ratsimandresy et al., 2017)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: POP3 appeared to interact with ASC as favorably as POP1 at the bottom interfaces.
source: POP3, on the other hand, appeared to interact with ASC as favorably as POP1 at the bottom interfaces (Figure 1B; ∆G=–34.3 for POP1•ASCPYD vs. ∆G=−34.6 for POP3•ASCPYD)
evidence: This statement is based on Rosetta interface analysis data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: POP3 could also inhibit the central adaptor ASC.
source: POP3, on the other hand, appeared to interact with ASC as favorably as POP1 at the bottom interfaces (Figure 1B; ∆G=–34.3 for POP1•ASCPYD vs. ∆G=−34.6 for POP3•ASCPYD), suggesting that it could also inhibit the central adaptor.
evidence: This is an inference based on Rosetta interface analysis data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: All three POPs showed comparable overall ∆Gs on the bottom half for AIM2PYD.
source: For AIM2PYD, all three POPs showed comparable overall ∆Gs on the bottom half (Figure 1C)
evidence: This statement is based on Rosetta interface analysis data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Each of the three POPs could target AIM2.
source: For AIM2PYD, all three POPs showed comparable overall ∆Gs on the bottom half (Figure 1C), which suggested that each of them could target AIM2.
evidence: This is an inference based on Rosetta interface analysis data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: IFI16 favored POP3 the most.
source: IFI16 favored POP3 the most (Figure 1D; e.g. ∆G=–9.6 for POP3•IFI16PYD on the top half)
evidence: This statement is based on Rosetta interface analysis data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: POP1 and POP2 might also recognize IFI16.
source: however, the other two POPs still showed more favorable ∆Gs than homotypic IFI16PYD•IFI16PYD interactions on at least one individual interface (Figure 1D; e.g. Type 2a for POP1, Type 2b for POP2, and Type 1b for POP3). These results in turn suggested that not only POP3, but POP1 and POP2 might also recognize IFI16.
evidence: This is an inference based on Rosetta interface analysis data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: POPs interfere with the recruitment of ASC by the upstream receptors.
source: It has been speculated that POPs interfere with the recruitment of ASC by the upstream receptors (de Almeida et al., 2015; Devi et al., 2020; Indramohan et al., 2018; Periasamy et al., 2017; Ratsimandresy et al., 2017)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: It remains unknown whether POPs directly inhibit NLRPs.
source: It has been speculated that POPs interfere with the recruitment of ASC by the upstream receptors (de Almeida et al., 2015; Devi et al., 2020; Indramohan et al., 2018; Periasamy et al., 2017; Ratsimandresy et al., 2017); however, it remains unknown whether they do so by directly inhibiting NLRPs, which are the major class of inflammasome receptors.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in knowledge based on prior research.

claim: POP1 could interact with NLRP3PYD on the top half.
source: Our Rosetta analyses here suggest that POP1 could interact with NLRP3PYD on the top half (Figure 1E; ∆G=–31.4 for NLRP3PYD•NLRP3PYD vs. ∆G=−30.5 for POP1•NLRP3PYD).
evidence: This is an inference based on Rosetta interface analysis data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The interactions between POP2/3 and NLRP3PYD appeared much less favorable.
source: However, the interactions between POP2/3 and NLRP3PYD appeared much less favorable (Figure 1E).
evidence: This statement is based on Rosetta interface analysis data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: POP1 showed more favorable energy scores toward NLRP6PYD than POP2/3.
source: Similar to NLRP3PYD, POP1 again showed more favorable energy scores toward NLRP6PYD than POP2/3 (Figure 1F).
evidence: This statement is based on Rosetta interface analysis data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: When ectopically expressed in HEK293T cells, C-terminally mCherry-tagged ASCPYD forms filaments.
source: When ectopically expressed in HEK293T cells, C-terminally mCherry-tagged ASCPYD forms filaments and full-length ASC (ASCFL) forms puncta (Matyszewski et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Full-length ASC (ASCFL) forms puncta when ectopically expressed in HEK293T cells.
source: When ectopically expressed in HEK293T cells, C-terminally mCherry-tagged ASCPYD forms filaments and full-length ASC (ASCFL) forms puncta (Matyszewski et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: HEK293T cells do not contain any endogenous inflammasome components or POPs.
source: Importantly, HEK293T cells do not contain any endogenous inflammasome components or POPs, providing an ideal cellular system for directly tracking their interactions (de Almeida et al., 2015; Matyszewski et al., 2021; Shi et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: POP1-eGFP only marginally inhibited the filament assembly of ASCPYD-mCherry (≤20% suppression vs. eGFP control).
source: Compared to co-transfecting eGFP alone, POP1-eGFP only marginally inhibited the filament assembly of ASCPYD-mCherry (≤20% suppression vs. eGFP control; Figure 2A–B).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from cellular imaging assays shown in Figure 2A–B.

claim: Co-transfecting POP2-eGFP or POP3-eGFP significantly reduced the amount of ASCPYD-mCherry filaments, with POP2 being more effective.
source: By contrast, co-transfecting POP2-eGFP or POP3-eGFP significantly reduced the amount of ASCPYD-mCherry filaments, with POP2 being more effective (Figure 2A–B; note more diffused mCherry signals and reduction in linear filaments in the presence of POP2 and POP3 in Figure 2A).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from cellular imaging assays shown in Figure 2A–B.

claim: POP1 reduced the number of ASCFL puncta by ~30%.
source: Furthermore, POP1 reduced the number of ASCFL puncta by ~30%, yet POP2 and POP3 were again more effective in preventing punctum formation (up to ~80% reduction, Figure 2C–D).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from cellular imaging assays shown in Figure 2C–D.

claim: POP2 and POP3 were more effective than POP1 in preventing ASCFL punctum formation (up to ~80% reduction).
source: Furthermore, POP1 reduced the number of ASCFL puncta by ~30%, yet POP2 and POP3 were again more effective in preventing punctum formation (up to ~80% reduction, Figure 2C–D).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from cellular imaging assays shown in Figure 2C–D.

claim: POPs suppress filament assembly altogether, unlike COPs that co-assemble with CARDs into filaments.
source: These results suggest that POP1 may not directly target ASCPYD. Moreover, unlike COPs that co-assemble with CARDs into filaments (Lu et al., 2016), our observations indicate that POPs suppress filament assembly altogether.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data and comparison with prior research on COPs.

claim: Recombinant POP1 behaved as a monomer without forming filaments or higher-order species.
source: POP1 behaved as a monomer without forming filaments or higher-order species in our hands (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–B).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from SEC and nsEM shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–B.

claim: Recombinant POP2 and POP3 were prone to aggregation/degradation during purification and required an N-terminal maltose-binding protein (MBP) tag to obtain intact proteins.
source: On the other hand, recombinant POP2 and POP3 were prone to aggregation/degradation during purification and required an N-terminal maltose-binding protein (MBP) tag to obtain intact proteins (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from SEC shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Cleaving MBP via tobacco etch virus protease (TEVp) indicated that POP2 and POP3 form elongated oligomers with undefined structures.
source: Cleaving MBP via tobacco etch virus protease (TEVp) indicated that POP2 and POP3 form elongated oligomers with undefined structures (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from nsEM shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: POP1 did not affect the oligomerization kinetics or maximum FRET efficiency (amplitude) of ASCPYD up to 150 µM.
source: Consistent with our cellular imaging assays (Figure 2A–B), POP1 did not affect the oligomerization kinetics or maximum FRET efficiency (amplitude) of ASCPYD up to the highest concentration we could achieve (Figure 2E; 150 µM POP1 vs. 2.5 µM ASCPYD).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from FRET assays shown in Figure 2E.

claim: No FRET signals were detected between donor-labeled POP1 and acceptor-labeled ASCPYD.
source: Moreover, no FRET signals were detected between donor-labeled POP1 and acceptor-labeled ASCPYD (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from FRET assays shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: The presence of POP1 did not affect the formation of ASCPYD filaments when visualized with negative-stain electron microscopy (nsEM).
source: Additionally, the presence of POP1 did not affect the formation of ASCPYD filaments when visualized with negative-stain electron microscopy (nsEM) (Figure 2F).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from nsEM shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Both POP2 and POP3 prolonged the initial lag phase of ASCPYD polymerization in a dose-dependent manner (up to ~15 min delay in nucleation).
source: By contrast, both POP2 and POP3 prolonged the initial lag phase of ASCPYD polymerization in a dose-dependent manner (up to ~15 min delay in nucleation; Figure 2E)
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from FRET assays shown in Figure 2E.

claim: POP2 and POP3 moderately affected the elongation phase of ASCPYD polymerization (≤20% reduction in the slope).
source: By contrast, both POP2 and POP3 prolonged the initial lag phase of ASCPYD polymerization in a dose-dependent manner (up to ~15 min delay in nucleation; Figure 2E), while also moderately affecting the elongation phase (≤20% reduction in the slope; Figure 2E).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from FRET assays shown in Figure 2E.

claim: POP2 and POP3 are similarly effective in suppressing the oligomerization of ASCPYD (IC50s).
source: Estimating the polymerization half-times at different POP concentrations indicated that POP2 and POP3 are similarly effective in suppressing the oligomerization of ASCPYD (Figure 2E, IC50s).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from FRET assays shown in Figure 2E.

claim: No ASCPYD filaments were detected in the presence of POP2 when visualized via nsEM.
source: When visualized via nsEM, no ASCPYD filaments were detected in the presence of POP2, and only a few filaments were seen with POP3 (Figure 2F).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from nsEM shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Only a few ASCPYD filaments were seen with POP3 when visualized via nsEM.
source: When visualized via nsEM, no ASCPYD filaments were detected in the presence of POP2, and only a few filaments were seen with POP3 (Figure 2F).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from nsEM shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Even if ASCPYDs form oligomers, most of them fail to assemble into intact filaments in the presence of POP2/3.
source: These results suggest that even if ASCPYDs form oligomers (rise in FRET signals in Figure 2E), most of them fail to assemble into intact filaments in the presence of POP2/3.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data from FRET assays and nsEM shown in Figure 2E and 2F.

claim: The complete absence of any ASCPYD filaments in the presence of POP2 is consistent with cellular experiments in which POP2 was most potent in inhibiting the central adaptor.
source: Moreover, the complete absence of any ASCPYD filaments in the presence of POP2 is consistent with our cellular experiments in which POP2 was most potent in inhibiting the central adaptor (Figure 2B and F).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data from nsEM and cellular imaging shown in Figure 2B and 2F.

claim: Both POP2 and POP3 impede the nucleation of the ASCPYD filament.
source: We also find that both POP2 and POP3 impede the nucleation of the ASCPYD filament.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from FRET assays.

claim: All three POPs contain favorable protein•protein interaction surfaces for ASCPYD (∆∆G = ∆GPYD•PYD- ∆GPOP•PYD ≤3.5).
source: For instance, all three POPs contain favorable protein•protein interaction surfaces for ASCPYD (∆∆G = ∆GPYD•PYD- ∆GPOP•PYD ≤3.5; arbitrarily determined, marked as blue dots in Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This statement is based on Rosetta interface analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Both POP2 and POP3 show multiple interfaces with less favorable ∆Gs than ASCPYD•ASPYD interactions, but POP1•ASCPYD interfaces lack such negative interactions.
source: However, although both POP2 and POP3 show multiple interfaces with less favorable ∆Gs than ASCPYD•ASPYD interactions, POP1•ASCPYD interfaces lack such negative interactions (∆∆G≥10.0; marked as red dots in Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This statement is based on Rosetta interface analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: A combination of favorable (recognition) and unfavorable interfaces (repulsion) is necessary for POPs to interfere with the assembly of inflammasome PYDs.
source: These observations in turn raised the hypothesis that a combination of favorable (recognition) and unfavorable interfaces (repulsion) is necessary for POPs to interfere with the assembly of inflammasome PYDs.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on Rosetta interface analysis data.

claim: There is a mixture of both favorable and unfavorable interactions between all three POPs and both ALRs (AIM2 and IFI16).
source: Here, we noted a mixture of both favorable and unfavorable interactions between all three POPs and both ALRs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–B)
evidence: This statement is based on Rosetta interface analysis data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–B.

claim: Not only POP3, but the other two POPs might also inhibit the oligomerization of ALRs.
source: Here, we noted a mixture of both favorable and unfavorable interactions between all three POPs and both ALRs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–B), raising the possibility that not only POP3, but the other two POPs might also inhibit the oligomerization of ALRs.
evidence: This is an inference based on Rosetta interface analysis data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–B.

claim: POP1 was more effective in suppressing the filament assembly by AIM2PYD and IFI16PYD than that of ASCPYD.
source: Compared to co-transfecting with eGFP alone, POP1-eGFP reduced the number of AIM2PYD and IFI16PYD filaments, apparently more effective than against ASCPYD (Figure 2B vs. Figure 3B and D; e.g. at 1200 ng POP1, AIM2PYD and IFI16PYD assemblies were inhibited ~60%, while ASCPYD assembly was suppressed ~20%).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from cellular imaging assays shown in Figure 2B and Figure 3B and D.

claim: Co-transfecting POP2 or POP3 essentially obliterated the filament assembly of AIM2PYD and IFI16PYD.
source: On the other hand, co-transfecting POP2 or POP3 essentially obliterated the filament assembly of AIM2PYD and IFI16PYD (Figure 3A–B and C–D).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from cellular imaging assays shown in Figure 3A–B and C–D.

claim: Recombinant IFI16PYD does not form filaments in our hands.
source: In our FRET assays tracking AIM2PYD polymerization, all three POPs decreased the slope of the linear phase in a dose-dependent manner without affecting the initial lag phase (Figure 3E; recombinant IFI16PYD does not form filaments in our hands; Morrone et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental observations and a citation to prior research.

claim: All three POPs can interfere with the elongation of the AIM2PYD filament, with POP3 being most effective.
source: Our observations indicate that all three POPs can interfere with the elongation of the AIM2PYD filament, with POP3 being most effective (Figure 3E, IC50s).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from FRET assays shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Imaging AIM2PYD filaments using nsEM in the presence of POP1 revealed that the filaments are shorter and fewer.
source: Moreover, imaging AIM2PYD filaments using nsEM in the presence of POP1 revealed that the filaments are shorter and fewer, and the presence of POP2/3 abrogated filament formation (Figure 3F).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from nsEM shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The presence of POP2/3 abrogated AIM2PYD filament formation.
source: Moreover, imaging AIM2PYD filaments using nsEM in the presence of POP1 revealed that the filaments are shorter and fewer, and the presence of POP2/3 abrogated filament formation (Figure 3F).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from nsEM shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The dearth of filaments in the presence of POP2/3 indicated that AIM2PYD oligomers rarely progressed into functional filaments.
source: As seen from ASCPYD, the dearth of filaments in the presence of POP2/3 in our nsEM and in cellulo experiments (Figure 3B, D and F) indicated that AIM2PYD oligomers rarely progressed into functional filaments (i.e. rise in FRET signals in Figure 3E vs. the lack of filaments in Figure 3F).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data from FRET assays and nsEM shown in Figure 3E and 3F.

claim: The oligomerization of PYD is important for stable dsDNA binding by ALRs.
source: It is noteworthy that the oligomerization of PYD is important for stable dsDNA binding by ALRs (Morrone et al., 2015; Morrone et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Although isolated AIM2PYD can form filaments by mass action, dsDNA provides a one-dimensional diffusion scaffold to facilitate the assembly of full-length ALRs at significantly lower concentrations.
source: Conversely, although isolated AIM2PYD can form filaments by mass action (i.e. high concentrations; Morrone et al., 2015), dsDNA provides a one-dimensional diffusion scaffold to facilitate the assembly of full-length ALRs at significantly lower concentrations (Morrone et al., 2015; Morrone et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: AIM2FL forms punctum-like oligomers when transfected in HEK293T cells.
source: AIM2FL forms punctum-like oligomers when transfected in HEK293T cells (Matyszewski et al., 2021)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: POP1 slightly reduced the number of AIM2FL puncta, while POP2 and POP3 were more effective.
source: AIM2FL forms punctum-like oligomers when transfected in HEK293T cells (Matyszewski et al., 2021), and we found that POP1 slightly reduced the number of AIM2FL puncta, while POP2 and POP3 were more effective (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from cellular imaging assays shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–D.

claim: IFI16FL localizes in the nucleus.
source: IFI16FL localizes in the nucleus (Antiochos et al., 2018; Kerur et al., 2011; Li et al., 2012)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: POP1 failed to interfere with dsDNA-binding/oligomerization of recombinant AIM2FL.
source: Consistent with the lack of significant inhibition in cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–D), POP1 failed to interfere with dsDNA-binding/oligomerization of recombinant AIM2FL (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from dsDNA binding assays shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: POP2 and POP3 inhibited the dsDNA binding of AIM2.
source: However, POP2 and POP3 still inhibited the dsDNA binding of AIM2, while only POP3 was inhibitory toward the dsDNA binding of recombinant IFI16FL (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from dsDNA binding assays shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Only POP3 was inhibitory toward the dsDNA binding of recombinant IFI16FL.
source: However, POP2 and POP3 still inhibited the dsDNA binding of AIM2, while only POP3 was inhibitory toward the dsDNA binding of recombinant IFI16FL (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from dsDNA binding assays shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: POP3 directly inhibits ALR assembly (elongation in particular for AIM2PYD).
source: Overall, our results indicate that POP3 directly inhibits ALR assembly (elongation in particular for AIM2PYD).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from FRET assays and nsEM.

claim: POP1 and POP2 can inhibit the assembly of ALR filaments, with POP2 being more effective than the former.
source: We also find that POP1 and POP2 can inhibit the assembly of ALR filaments, with POP2 being more effective than the former
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from cellular imaging, FRET assays, and nsEM.

claim: The presence of activating ligands can diminish the inhibitory effect of POPs.
source: the presence of activating ligands can diminish the inhibitory effect of POPs (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from dsDNA binding assays shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: POP1 can make a combination of favorable and unfavorable interactions with both NLRP3PYD and NLRP6PYD.
source: Indeed, our Rosetta analyses indicated that POP1 can make a combination of favorable and unfavorable interactions with both NLRP3PYD and NLRP6PYD (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is based on Rosetta interface analysis data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: POP2 and POP3 also showed favorable and unfavorable interactions with NLRP3.
source: Furthermore, POP2 and POP3 also showed favorable and unfavorable interactions with NLRP3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This statement is based on Rosetta interface analysis data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The Type 3a surface of NLRP6 showed an energy score that might allow POP2/3 to recognize NLRP6 if present at high enough concentrations.
source: although the ∆Gs between NLRP6 and POP2/3 were largely unfavorable, the Type 3a surface showed an energy score that might allow the two POPs to recognize NLRP6 if present at high enough concentrations (∆G ~ –9; Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, marked as light pink)
evidence: This is an inference based on Rosetta interface analysis data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The activation mechanisms of NLRPs are complex and involve different types of active and inactive oligomers.
source: The activation mechanisms of NLRPs are complex and involve different types of active and inactive oligomers (Andreeva et al., 2021; Gong et al., 2021; Hochheiser et al., 2022b; Lu et al., 2014; Ohto et al., 2022; Sharif et al., 2019; Sharma and de Alba, 2021; Shen et al., 2021; Shen et al., 2019)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: NLRP2PYD-mCherry did not form filaments when expressed in HEK293T cells.
source: Of note, NLRP2PYD-mCherry did not form filaments when expressed in HEK293T cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from cellular imaging shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: POP1 was more effective in suppressing the filament assembly by both NLRP3PYD and NLRP6PYD than that of ASCPYD.
source: When co-transfected, POP1 was more effective in suppressing the filament assembly by both NLRP3PYD and NLRP6PYD than that of ASCPYD (Figure 4A–D). For example, with 1200 ng POP1, ASCPYD assembly was only suppressed by ~20%, but the filament assembly by NLRP3PYD and NLRP6PYD was suppressed ~60% (Figure 2B vs. Figure 4B and D).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from cellular imaging assays shown in Figure 2B and Figure 4B and D.

claim: POP2 was less effective in inhibiting the polymerization of NLRPPYDs than that of ASCPYD.
source: On the other hand, POP2 was less effective in inhibiting the polymerization of NLRPPYDs than that of ASCPYD (e.g. at 600 ng POP2, ASCPYD assembly was abolished, but the assembly of NLRP3PYD and NLRP6PYD was minimally suppressed; Figure 2B vs. Figure 4B and D).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from cellular imaging assays shown in Figure 2B and Figure 4B and D.

claim: POP3 was almost equally effective in suppressing the polymerization of NLRPPYDs and ASCPYD, but not nearly as effective as against ALRs.
source: POP3 was almost equally effective in suppressing the polymerization of NLRPPYDs and ASCPYD, but not nearly as effective as against ALRs (Figure 4A–D). For example, at 600 ng POP3, AIM2PYD assembly was suppressed 70%, but those of ASCPYD and NLRPPYDs were reduced by 40–50%; Figure 3B vs. Figures 2B, 4B and D.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from cellular imaging assays shown in Figure 2B, Figure 3B, and Figure 4B and D.

claim: POP1 predominantly inhibited the elongation of NLRP6PYD filament.
source: POP1 predominantly inhibited the elongation of NLRP6PYD filament, and POP2 appeared to interfere with its nucleation.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from FRET assays.

claim: POP2 appeared to interfere with the nucleation of NLRP6PYD filament.
source: POP1 predominantly inhibited the elongation of NLRP6PYD filament, and POP2 appeared to interfere with its nucleation.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from FRET assays.

claim: POP3 mostly reduced the elongation kinetics of NLRP6PYD, but it also seemed to interfere with nucleation.
source: Although POP3 mostly reduced the elongation kinetics of NLRP6PYD, it also seemed to interfere with nucleation (Figure 4E).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from FRET assays shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The number and length of NLRP6PYD filaments were reduced in the presence of POPs.
source: Consistent with these observations, the number and length of NLRP6PYD filaments were reduced in the presence of POPs (Figure 4E).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from nsEM shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The lack of filaments despite the increase in FRET signals indicates that NLRP6PYD oligomers fail to form intact filaments.
source: The lack of filaments (Figure 4F) despite the increase in FRET signals (Figure 4E) again indicates that NLRP6PYD oligomers fail to form intact filaments.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data from FRET assays and nsEM shown in Figure 4E and 4F.

claim: POP2 was most effective in suppressing IL-18 release, POP3 was the second, and POP1 was least effective.
source: Consistent with our imaging and polymerization assays, here, POP2 was most effective in suppressing IL-18 release, POP3 was the second, and POP1 was least effective (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from IL-18 release assays shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2E.

claim: POP1 acts as a decoy ASC, moderately inhibiting the assembly of upstream PYDs.
source: Our results are consistent with the idea that POP1 acts as a decoy ASC, moderately inhibiting the assembly of upstream PYDs
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data from cellular imaging, FRET assays, and nsEM.

claim: POP2 is the most potent inhibitor of inflammasomes.
source: POP2 is the most potent inhibitor of inflammasomes
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data from cellular imaging, FRET assays, and IL-18 release assays.

claim: POP3 can inhibit inflammasomes beyond AIM2.
source: POP3 can inhibit inflammasomes beyond AIM2.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data from cellular imaging, FRET assays, and nsEM.

claim: N73L-AIM2PYD and D23K-AIM2PYD were impaired in filament assembly.
source: Both N73L-AIM2PYD and D23K-AIM2PYD were impaired in filament assembly (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from nsEM shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Imaging WT-AIM2PYD filaments using nsEM in the presence of N73L mutant showed fewer filaments.
source: Imaging WT-AIM2PYD filaments using nsEM in the presence of either mutant showed fewer filaments (N73L) and mesh-like non-filamentous aggregates (D23K; Figure 5B).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from nsEM shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Imaging WT-AIM2PYD filaments using nsEM in the presence of D23K mutant showed mesh-like non-filamentous aggregates.
source: Imaging WT-AIM2PYD filaments using nsEM in the presence of either mutant showed fewer filaments (N73L) and mesh-like non-filamentous aggregates (D23K; Figure 5B).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from nsEM shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The presence of unlabeled N73L-AIM2PYD or D23K-AIM2PYD impeded the polymerization of WT-AIM2PYD in FRET assay, with the former being more effective.
source: The presence of unlabeled N73L-AIM2PYD or D23K-AIM2PYD also impeded the polymerization of WT-AIM2PYD in our FRET assay, with the former being more effective (Figure 5C).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from FRET assays shown in Figure 5C.

claim: When co-transfected in HEK293T cells, eGFP-tagged AIM2PYD mutants diminished the number of mCherry-tagged WT filaments, again N73L being more effective than D23K.
source: Moreover, when co-transfected in HEK293T cells, eGFP-tagged AIM2PYD mutants diminished the number of mCherry-tagged WT filaments, again N73L being more effective than D23K (Figure 5D–E, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–C).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from cellular imaging assays shown in Figure 5D–E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–C.

claim: PYDs can be reprogrammed into POP-like inhibitors even by a single mutation.
source: Our results also provide a proof of principle that PYDs can be reprogrammed into POP-like inhibitors even by a single mutation.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data from cellular imaging, FRET assays, and nsEM.

claim: ASC promotes 'solidification' of inflammasomes in a prion-like manner, allowing them to perpetuate even after cells undergo pyroptosis.
source: For example, ASC promotes 'solidification' of inflammasomes in a prion-like manner, allowing them to perpetuate even after cells undergo pyroptosis (Cai et al., 2014; Franklin et al., 2014; Shen et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: AIM2 and IFI16 filaments persist and are even stigmatized as autoantigens in debilitating autoimmune disorders such as systemic lupus erythematosus and Sjögren's syndrome.
source: Moreover, AIM2 and IFI16 filaments also persist and are even stigmatized as autoantigens in debilitating autoimmune disorders such as systemic lupus erythematosus and Sjögren's syndrome (Antiochos et al., 2018; Antiochos et al., 2022; Baer et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Persisting inflammasome oligomers and their aberrant activities are implicated in a wide range of human diseases including COVID-19.
source: Indeed, persisting inflammasome oligomers and their aberrant activities are implicated in a wide range of human diseases including COVID-19 (Karki et al., 2017; Tartey and Kanneganti, 2020; Vora et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: POPs interfere with the polymerization (nucleation and/or elongation) of various inflammasome filaments without co-assembling.
source: Our investigations here reveal that POPs interfere with the polymerization (nucleation and/or elongation) of various inflammasome filaments without co-assembling, which is different from COPs that co-assemble into filaments with CARD of caspase-1 (Lu et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from FRET assays and nsEM, and comparison with prior research on COPs.

claim: Excess POPs were necessary to inhibit inflammasome PYDs, especially when an activating ligand was present.
source: Moreover, also unlike COPs that can inhibit the assembly of pro-caspases at sub-stoichiometric concentrations (Lu et al., 2016), excess POPs were necessary to inhibit inflammasome PYDs, especially when an activating ligand was present (dsDNA for AIM2 and IFI16; Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from FRET assays and dsDNA binding assays, and comparison with prior research on COPs.

claim: POP2/3 largely suppressed the nucleation of ASC.
source: Additionally, POP2/3 largely suppressed the nucleation of ASC (e.g. prolonged lags in Figure 2E)
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from FRET assays shown in Figure 2E.

claim: POP2/3 interfered with the elongation of upstream receptors.
source: yet these POPs also interfered with the elongation of upstream receptors (e.g. Figures 3E and 4E).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from FRET assays shown in Figures 3E and 4E.

claim: Being able to modulate two key assembly steps (nucleation and elongation) while requiring excess POPs is well suited for attenuating inflammasome activities without shutting them down altogether.
source: We reason that being able to modulate two key assembly steps (nucleation and elongation) while requiring excess POPs is well suited for attenuating inflammasome activities without shutting them down altogether.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on experimental data.

claim: The expression of POP1 is predominantly induced by IL-1β.
source: It is noteworthy that the expression of POP1 is predominantly induced by IL-1β (de Almeida et al., 2015), a major final product of inflammasome cascades (Broz and Dixit, 2016; Zheng et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: POP1 is likely part of a negative feedback loop for attenuating excessive inflammasome activities by preventing perpetuation of upstream filaments.
source: Thus, it is likely that POP1 is part of a negative feedback loop for attenuating excessive inflammasome activities by preventing perpetuation of upstream filaments (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on experimental data and prior knowledge.

claim: POP2 is thought to function similarly to POP1 by suppressing the activation of ASC.
source: POP2 is thought to function similarly to POP1 by suppressing the activation of ASC (Periasamy et al., 2017; Ratsimandresy et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: POP2 is reportedly more effective than POP1 in preventing spurious inflammasome activities in vivo.
source: Interestingly, POP2 is reportedly more effective than POP1 in preventing spurious inflammasome activities in vivo (Periasamy et al., 2017; Ratsimandresy et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: POP2 can potently inhibit the nucleation of ASCPYD while moderately suppressing the oligomerization of select upstream receptors such as AIM2.
source: We find here that POP2 can indeed potently inhibit the nucleation of ASCPYD (Figure 2) while moderately suppressing the oligomerization of select upstream receptors such as AIM2.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from FRET assays and cellular imaging shown in Figure 2.

claim: The expression of POP2 is readily induced by a wide variety of pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines.
source: It is noteworthy that the expression of POP2 is readily induced by a wide variety of pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines (Ratsimandresy et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: POP2 would act as the pan-inflammasome inhibitor essential for preventing spurious innate immune responses.
source: Considering that it primarily targets ASC, we postulate that POP2 would act as the pan-inflammasome inhibitor essential for preventing spurious innate immune responses (Figure 6; i.e. decoy receptor as it is most similar to upstream NLRP2PYD, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on experimental data and prior knowledge.

claim: POP3 was identified as a selective inflammasome inhibitor targeting ALRs.
source: POP3 was identified as a selective inflammasome inhibitor targeting ALRs (Khare et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: In addition to inhibiting the elongation of the AIM2PYD filament, POP3 can robustly inhibit the nucleation of ASCPYD.
source: In addition to inhibiting the elongation of the AIM2PYD filament, we find here that POP3 can robustly inhibit the nucleation of ASCPYD (Figure 2)
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from FRET assays shown in Figure 2.

claim: In principle, POP3 can inhibit the assembly of NLRPPYDs.
source: We also find that, in principle, POP3 can inhibit the assembly of NLRPPYDs (Figure 4).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from cellular imaging and FRET assays shown in Figure 4.

claim: POP3 is exclusively induced by interferons (IFNs).
source: Unlike the other two POPs, POP3 is exclusively induced by interferons (IFNs) (Khare et al., 2014)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: IFNs also drive the expression of ALRs.
source: Considering that IFNs also drive the expression of ALRs (Antiochos et al., 2018; Khare et al., 2014)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Although POP3 is intrinsically capable of inhibiting various inflammasome receptors, the contextual expression would dictate its in vivo targets.
source: we postulate that although POP3 is intrinsically capable of inhibiting various inflammasome receptors, the contextual expression would dictate its in vivo targets (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on experimental data and prior knowledge.

claim: The nonequilibrium assembly of inflammasome filaments plays a major role in defining the mechanism of regulation by POPs.
source: We envision that the nonequilibrium assembly of inflammasome filaments plays a major role in defining the mechanism of regulation by POPs (i.e. kinetically driven without having conceivable off-rates) (Cai et al., 2014; Matyszewski et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on experimental data and prior knowledge.

claim: All POP and PYD protomers share the same overall structure (shape complementarity).
source: For instance, considering that all POP and PYD protomers share the same overall structure (shape complementarity)
evidence: This statement is based on established structural knowledge of PYDs and POPs.

claim: Any (semi) favorable protein•protein interaction interfaces would allow POPs and PYDs to associate at least transiently.
source: we reason that any (semi) favorable protein•protein interaction interfaces would allow POPs and PYDs to associate at least transiently (i.e. classic reversible protein•protein interaction equilibrium).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on protein-protein interaction principles.

claim: The more favorable homotypic PYD•PYD interactions would readily outcompete meta-stable POP•PYD interactions especially when only basal amounts of POPs are present.
source: However, the more favorable homotypic PYD•PYD interactions would readily outcompete such meta-stable interactions especially when only basal amounts of POPs are present (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on Rosetta interface analysis data and protein-protein interaction principles.

claim: If POPs do not contain any strong unfavorable interactions against target PYDs, homotypic PYD•PYD interactions would still outcompete even excess POPs and lock themselves into irreversible filament assembly.
source: Moreover, as indicated from the failure to inhibit ASCPYD by POP1, if POPs do not contain any strong unfavorable interactions against target PYDs, homotypic PYD•PYD interactions would still outcompete even excess POPs and lock themselves into irreversible filament assembly (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on experimental data and protein-protein interaction principles.

claim: When meta-stable POP•PYD complexes contain at least one very unfavorable interface, excess POPs would expose a multitude of adverse protein•protein interaction surfaces that would hamper filament assembly.
source: However, when such meta-stable POP•PYD complexes contain at least one very unfavorable interface, excess POPs would then expose a multitude of adverse protein•protein interaction surfaces that would hamper filament assembly (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on experimental data and protein-protein interaction principles.

claim: Multimeric POPs are more effective in preventing the association of inflammasome PYDs.
source: Also of note, given that POP2 and POP3 can form oligomers (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–B), it is highly likely that multimeric POPs are more effective in preventing the association of inflammasome PYDs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on experimental data.

claim: The recognition between AIM2 and ASC occurs when at least one is filamentous.
source: We found previously that the recognition between AIM2 and ASC occurs when at least one is filamentous (Matyszewski et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: POPs might preferentially interact with oligomeric PYDs that are not yet fully filamentous, trapping them into nonfunctional states.
source: Thus, it is also possible that POPs might preferentially interact with oligomeric PYDs that are not yet fully filamentous (e.g. (pseudo)-nucleation unit), trapping them into nonfunctional states (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on experimental data and prior knowledge.

claim: Although experiments using AIM2FL, IFI16FL, and NLRP3FL are consistent with those from isolated PYDs, there could be yet another layer of complexity in POP•inflammasome interactions beyond what has been reported.
source: In closing, a possible caveat of our study is that although our experiments using AIM2FL, IFI16FL, and NLRP3FL are consistent with those from isolated PYDs (Figure 3—figure supplements 1C, 2 and Figure 3—figure supplement 3E; Figure 4—figure supplement 2E), considering that inflammasome receptors contain multiple domains, there could be yet another layer of complexity in POP•inflammasome interactions beyond what we have reported here.
evidence: This is a speculative statement acknowledging potential limitations of the study.

claim: Instead of being dictated by a.a. sequence homology, degenerate-code-like target selection and inhibition mechanisms underpin the regulation of inflammasome assembly by POPs.
source: Together, we propose that, instead of being dictated by a.a. sequence homology, degenerate-code-like target selection and inhibition mechanisms underpin the regulation of inflammasome assembly by POPs.
evidence: This is a proposal based on experimental data and Rosetta analyses.
